model_review.title: Revision limit max attribute not enforced in validation
model_review.reproduction: 1. Open the page. 2. Enter a project name. 3. In 'Contracted revision rounds', enter 101 (or any number > 100). 4. Click 'Create project'. The form accepts it because validateCreateForm() only checks limit < 1, not limit > 100.
model_review.expected: Form should reject values > 100, matching the input's max attribute.
model_review.actual: Form accepts any positive integer, ignoring the max="100" constraint.
model_review.label: MODEL_REVIEW

model_review.title: Export filename can be empty or invalid if project name contains only special characters
model_review.reproduction: 1. Create a project with name "!!!" (or any string with no alphanumeric chars). 2. Click 'Export client-ready summary'. The downloaded file is named "-revision-summary.txt" (leading dash, no actual name).
model_review.expected: Filename should have a fallback (e.g., 'revision-summary.txt') when sanitization yields empty string.
model_review.actual: Sanitization regex replaces all non-alphanumeric with '-', then toLowerCase(), resulting in empty base name.
model_review.label: MODEL_REVIEW

model_review.title: Load function does not validate loaded data structure
model_review.reproduction: 1. In DevTools console, run: localStorage.setItem('revision-rounds-project', JSON.stringify({project: null, roundCount: 5, revisions: 'not-an-array'})); 2. Reload page. 3. The app shows project view with 'null' as project title, roundCount 5, and crashes when trying to render revisions (TypeError: revisions.forEach is not a function).
model_review.expected: Load should validate that project is an object with name/limit, roundCount is a number, revisions is an array; on failure, clear storage and show create view.
model_review.actual: Load trusts parsed JSON structure; malformed data breaks the UI.
model_review.label: MODEL_REVIEW

model_review.title: 'New project' button does not actually create a new project; it only switches views
model_review.reproduction: 1. Create a project 'Project A' with limit 3. 2. Log one revision. 3. Click 'New project' (back-btn). 4. Enter 'Project B' with limit 2 and click 'Create project'. 5. The previous project 'Project A' data is overwritten in localStorage, but the user might expect 'New project' to allow multiple projects side-by-side (README says 'switching projects retains the previous one in localStorage' but only one key exists).
model_review.expected: Either rename button to 'Back to setup' or implement multi-project support. Current behavior is confusing: 'New project' implies creation, but it's just a view switch that discards the current project on next create.
model_review.actual: Button shows create view but doesn't reset form to allow a second project without overwriting the first.
model_review.label: MODEL_REVIEW
